The test image shows a corn stalk cross-section with:
- Very dark/black outer rind
- White/cream pith center with some yellow tones
- Decomposed tissue visible
- Appears to be a stalk rot disease

The dark black rind with lighter interior is characteristic of Anthracnose stalk rot. Let me check the reference image.

The reference confirms Anthracnose stalk rot features: dark rind discoloration and shredded/deteriorated pith. The test image matches well — showing the classic cross-section with:
- **Shiny black outer rind** (hallmark of *Colletotrichum graminicola*)
- **White/cream pith** with tissue breakdown
- Stalk base rotting pattern

This is consistent with Anthracnose stalk rot and not Gibberella/Fusarium (which would show pink/red coloration) or Charcoal rot (scattered black sclerotia throughout pith).
